title: The specified inverse-image comparison respects finite coefficient extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and chosen uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism on schemes where $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $F=E,L$ and $W=X,Y$ put $R_{F,W}=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}$ on $R_{F,Y}$-module complexes, with scalar action transported through $c_F:g^{-1}R_{F,Y}\simeq R_{F,X}$, and $\kappa^{g,F}_K:G_FK\to Lg_F^*K$ for the SPECIFIED integral comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], part (b). Here $Lg_F^*$ is completed derived pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

Let $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and write $T_W$ for integral scalar extension to $\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. Use the natural isomorphism
$$\alpha_K:T_X(Lg_E^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_L^*(T_YK)$$
of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], with its canonical tensor and completion comparison (ordinary tensor associativity followed by the strict quotient-tower completion comparisons). For a derived-complete $H$ put $C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ and let $\chi_{W,H}:C_WH\xrightarrow{\sim}T_WH$ be the SPECIFIED completion comparison of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. The tensor isomorphism of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom], followed by $c_E,c_L$, gives
$$b_K:C_XG_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LC_YK,$$
whose local formula is $y\otimes a\mapsto g^{-1}(y_0\otimes a_0)$ when $y=g^{-1}y_0$ and $a=c_L(g^{-1}a_0)$. The inverse image is an exact equivalence [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], so this tensor identification also defines $b$ on derived categories. The objects $G_EK$ and $Lg_E^*K$ are constructible and derived complete [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback]. Define
$$\beta_K=G_L(\chi_{Y,K})\circ b_K\circ\chi_{X,G_EK}^{-1}:T_XG_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LT_YK.$$
Then the specified maps obey
$$\alpha_K\circ T_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}\circ\beta_K$$
in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), pp. 50-51 (completed pullback). The displayed compatibility of the specified comparison with coefficient extension is formulated by an agent from def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison(b); this formula is not a claim quoted from Bhatt-Scholze.

proof.text: The inverse-image equivalence for the scheme isomorphism is exact and commutes with all limits and colimits. The completed coefficient map used by the integral comparison is the map whose finite components satisfy π_m ∘ c_{O_E} = c^g_{A_{E,m}} ∘ g^{-1}(π_m), so it is compatible with every quotient transition. Hence the transported module functors G_E and G_L are exact on complexes and descend to the derived categories, while κ^{g,E} and κ^{g,L} are the specified maps of the comparison definition.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), together with the completed structure-map paragraph of def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison.

proof.text: Choose the K-flat representative P → K used to define the integral pullbacks. The inverse-image tensor comparison gives a chain-level map C_XG_EP → G_LC_YP by the pure-tensor rule y ⊗ a ↦ g^{-1}(y_0 ⊗ a_0), with the coefficient actions transported by c_E and c_L. The finite quotient maps commute with this rule, so it is a map of strict towers. Exactness of g^{-1} carries it through the localization and gives the derived isomorphism b_K : C_XG_EK → G_LC_YK.

source.place: Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4), tensor comparison on the chosen K-flat model.

proof.text: For every derived-complete $H$, the specified $\chi_{W,H}:C_WH\to T_WH$ is natural, independent of the K-flat resolution, and invertible. On a chosen resolution it is the quotient augmentation with zero shifted-product coordinate. Finite freeness of $S_W$ over $R_W$ means ordinary $C_W$ is termwise tensor on ANY complex; no K-flatness of a Roos cone is required to apply $C_W$. We will use naturality of this precise $\chi$ to replace $T_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)$ by $C_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)$ after conjugating by the two $\chi$ maps.

source.place: Agent calculation from the specified quotient-cone definitions, contextualized by Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4).

proof.text: Use $P\to K$ from Step 2 and the concrete flat-term K-flat $S_Y$-complex $Q=P\otimes_{R_{E,Y}}R_{L,Y}$; change of rings preserves K-flatness and flat terms. It represents $C_YK$, not the cone representing $T_YK$. The specified-map node defines $A_E(P)$, $A_L(Q)$, the same-index tower maps $d_m$ and their whole-cone map $\delta_P$. It gives $\alpha_K=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})[\delta_P]\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}^{-1}$. The chain map $\chi_Y(P):Q\to B(P)$ has the correct direction and represents $\chi_{Y,K}$; application of $Lg_L^*$ is in the derived category. Thus we have an explicit representative of the canonical tensor-and-completion comparison, refining the existence assertion in the scalar-operation lemma.

source.place: Agent calculation from the specified quotient-cone definitions, contextualized by Section 6.5, Lemma 6.5.9(4).

proof.text: The definition β_K = G_L(χ_{Y,K}) ∘ b_K ∘ χ_{X,G_EK}^{-1} is a composite of the three displayed isomorphisms. Therefore β_K is an isomorphism in D(X_proet,O_L), and its source and target are exactly T_XG_EK and G_LT_YK by the definitions of C and T.

We may compute the specified $\kappa^{g,L}_{C_YK}$ using $Q$ and move it along $\chi_{Y,K}$ to the specified $\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}$. The normalization lemma (applied with coefficient field $L$) gives $\theta_{g,N}\kappa^{g,L}_N=G_L(u_N)$ with $\theta_{g,N}$ an isomorphism, independent of the K-flat representative and natural for derived morphisms, and $u$ the natural completion unit. Hence $\kappa^{g,L}_N=\theta_{g,N}^{-1}G_L(u_N)$ is itself independent of the representative, and for a derived morphism $v:N\to N'$, $Lg_L^*(v)\kappa_N=\theta_{N'}^{-1}G_L(\widehat v)G_L(u_N)=\theta_{N'}^{-1}G_L(u_{N'})G_L(v)=\kappa_{N'}G_L(v)$. With $v=\chi_{Y,K}$ this gives the equality of actual derived maps
$$Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\,\kappa^{g,L}_{C_YK}=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}\,G_L(\chi_{Y,K}).$$
Here $C_YK$ is derived complete by the finite-free comparison. Naturality is applied on the ambient completed-module derived category, so it also applies to the cone model $B(P)$ and to any fixed K-flat re-resolution used in the definition of $\kappa_{T_YK}$.

proof.text:
Compute on the genuine tensor complex $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_{E,X}}R_{L,X}$, representing $C_XG_EK$. The left chain map is $\delta_P\circ(C_X\tilde\theta^E_P)$ and the right is $\tilde\theta^L_Q\circ b_P$, both landing in $A_L(Q)$. Take a local tensor generator $y\otimes s$, with $y=g^{-1}p$ and $s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0)$. The $m$-component of the left augmentation first sends $y$ to $(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes1$ at E-level. The formula for $d_m$ sends its tensor with $s$ to
$$(g^{-1}(p\otimes1))\otimes\pi^L_m(s)\ \in g_{L,m}^*(Q_{L,m}).$$
The right route sends $y\otimes s$ by $b_P$ to $g^{-1}(p\otimes s_0)$, then reduces $Q$ and tensors with $1$. Balancing the sheaf tensor product moves $s_0$ to the last coefficient, giving exactly the same displayed element. Compatibility $\pi^L_m c_L=c^g_{A_{L,m}}g^{-1}(\pi^L_m)$ and functoriality of $c^g_A$ for $A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$ justify this balancing with the transported actions. The quotient maps commute with all transitions by their same-index definition. Both augmentations have shifted coordinate zero; $\delta_P$ applies $\prod d_m$ to BOTH coordinates and therefore sends that zero to zero. Thus the two chain maps to the entire cone coincide. After localization this is
$$[\delta_P]\,C_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)=\kappa^{g,L}_{C_YK}\,b_K.$$
The identification of the last $\kappa$ with the $Q$-representative uses Step 6; it does not assert that the cone $B(P)$ is K-flat.

proof.text:
Precompose the required square with the isomorphism $\chi_{X,G_EK}$. Naturality of $\chi$ and the formula of Step 4 give
$$\alpha_K T_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K)\chi_{X,G_EK}
= Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})[\delta_P]C_X(\kappa^{g,E}_K).$$
By Steps 7 and 6 this equals
$$Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\kappa^{g,L}_{C_YK}b_K
=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}G_L(\chi_{Y,K})b_K
=\kappa^{g,L}_{T_YK}\beta_K\chi_{X,G_EK}.$$
Cancel $\chi_{X,G_EK}$. These equalities take place in the localization of complexes; the only comparison inside a limit was already an equality of the entire cone maps in Step 7.
